$why: Tests that were RED at the measured baseline. A permanently failing test protects nothing — it is indistinguishable from a deleted one except that it costs time and memory, and it hides the tests that do work. Archived, not deleted: each file is intact, tracked in git, and restored by moving it back under test/. Every entry records what it was failing with, so a file can be triaged later without re-running the suite to find out.
$restoring: git mv test/archived/<path> test/<path> — then run the shard it belongs to.
